events.title: United States Declares War on Japan
events.description: The day after the Japanese attack on Pearl Harbor (December 7 in Hawaii), the U.S. Congress declared war on Japan with only one dissenting vote, and President Franklin D. Roosevelt signed the declaration. On the same day in Asia (December 8 local time), Japan attacked Malaya, Hong Kong, the Philippines, and other targets.
events.significance: Marked the formal entry of the United States into World War II, shifting the balance of global industrial and military power toward the Allies.

events.title: Assassination of John Lennon
events.description: Former Beatles member John Lennon was shot and killed outside the Dakota apartment building in New York City by Mark David Chapman. Lennon was 40 years old.
events.significance: His death triggered worldwide mourning and remains a defining moment in music history, strengthening his legacy as a cultural icon and peace advocate.

events.title: Belovezha Accords Signed
events.description: The leaders of Russia, Ukraine, and Belarus signed the Belovezha Accords, declaring that the Soviet Union had ceased to exist as a subject of international law and establishing the Commonwealth of Independent States.
events.significance: Effectively dissolved the Soviet Union, ending the Cold War era and reshaping the political map of Eurasia.

events.title: Proclamation of the Immaculate Conception
events.description: Pope Pius IX issued the apostolic constitution Ineffabilis Deus, defining as dogma that the Virgin Mary was conceived without original sin.
events.significance: It was a landmark moment in Roman Catholic doctrine and one of the few instances of a pope formally defining a dogma through papal authority.

events.title: INF Treaty Signed in Washington
events.description: U.S. President Ronald Reagan and Soviet leader Mikhail Gorbachev signed the Intermediate-Range Nuclear Forces (INF) Treaty at the White House, agreeing to eliminate an entire class of nuclear missiles.
events.significance: It was the first agreement between the superpowers to reduce, rather than merely limit, their nuclear arsenals, and it helped ease Cold War tensions.
